nodes.title: OSPF: Key Ideas
nodes.content: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state interior gateway protocol — every router floods its neighbors with link-state advertisements (LSAs), builds an identical map of the network, and runs Dijkstra to find shortest paths.

flashcards.front: What is an OSPF area, and why use multiple?
flashcards.back: An area is a group of OSPF routers that share full link-state info. ABRs (area border routers) summarize between areas. Single-area is fine for small networks (~50 routers); multi-area limits LSA flooding scope and reduces SPF computation as the network grows.

flashcards.front: What is area 0?
flashcards.back: The backbone area. All non-zero areas MUST connect to area 0, directly or via a virtual link. Inter-area traffic always passes through area 0. If area 0 partitions, OSPF breaks.

flashcards.front: Cost calculation — what's the formula?
flashcards.back: Default cost = reference-bandwidth ÷ interface-bandwidth. Reference defaults to 100 Mbps, so a 100 Mbps link costs 1, a 10 Mbps link costs 10. On modern networks you should raise the reference (e.g., to 1000) so 1G+ links get distinguishable costs.

flashcards.front: DR / BDR — what problem do they solve?
flashcards.back: On a multi-access segment (Ethernet), if every router formed a full adjacency with every other, you'd get O(n²) flooding. OSPF elects a Designated Router (DR) and Backup DR. Other routers only fully adjacency with the DR/BDR; the DR re-floods. The election uses priority then router ID.

pairs.stem: What is the difference between OSPF stub, totally stubby, and NSSA areas?
What is the OSPF default-information originate command?
pairs.option: Redistributes a default route (0.0.0.0/0) from the routing table into OSPF as a Type 5 External LSA — adds 'always' keyword to originate even without a default route in the routing table

pairs.stem: What is OSPF SPF (Shortest Path First) algorithm and when does it run?
What is OSPF area border router (ABR) behavior with multiple areas?
What is the purpose of route redistribution metric in OSPF?
What is the purpose of OSPF LSA Type 3 (Summary LSA)?
pairs.option: Generated by ABRs to advertise network prefixes from one area to other areas — allows inter-area routing while limiting full LSDB propagation across areas

nodes.title: Automation and IaC: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means defining your servers, networks, databases in version-controlled config files instead of clicking around a console. Pipelines automate the apply step. The combination is what makes cloud reproducible.

flashcards.front: What is the value of declarative IaC?
flashcards.back: You describe the desired state ('I want 3 EC2 instances in this VPC'), the tool figures out how to get there. Reruns are idempotent — applying the same code twice doesn't double anything. State drift (someone clicked in the console) is detected on the next plan/diff.

flashcards.front: Terraform vs CloudFormation vs Bicep — what's different?
flashcards.back: Terraform: cloud-agnostic, HCL syntax, plan/apply workflow, huge ecosystem. CloudFormation: AWS-only, YAML/JSON, native rollback. Bicep: Azure-only, cleaner DSL on top of ARM. Pick the cloud-native tool if you're single-cloud; Terraform if multi-cloud or your team prefers HCL.

flashcards.front: What is a CI/CD pipeline for infrastructure?
flashcards.back: Same as for app code: commit → run linter (tflint) → plan / diff → require approval → apply. Production typically has a manual approval gate; lower environments auto-apply. Plan output is reviewed in the PR so a destructive change is caught before merge.

flashcards.front: Why is mutable infrastructure considered an anti-pattern?
flashcards.back: Mutable: SSH in, run apt-get, edit configs, server drifts from its template. Two 'identical' servers slowly diverge → snowflakes → 'works on this instance only' bugs. Immutable: bake a fresh AMI / image, replace the running instance, the old one is destroyed. Painful upfront, trivial to roll back, no drift.

pairs.stem: What is Python's role in network automation?
pairs.option: The dominant programming language for network automation — used with libraries like Netmiko (SSH), NAPALM (multi-vendor), requests (REST APIs), nornir (framework), pyATS (Cisco testing)

pairs.stem: What is YANG and its role in network automation?
What is the purpose of RESTCONF/NETCONF in network automation?
What is Ansible in the context of network automation?
pairs.option: An agentless automation tool using SSH/NETCONF and YAML playbooks to configure network devices — no agent software needed on managed devices

pairs.stem: What is Cisco DNA Center and its role in Intent-Based Networking?
pairs.option: Cisco's central controller for network automation, providing design, provisioning, assurance, and policy enforcement across the campus network using intent-based networking principles

nodes.title: BGP: Key Ideas
nodes.content: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is the routing protocol of the internet. It runs between autonomous systems (ASes) and is a path-vector protocol — instead of a metric, each route carries the full list of ASes it has traversed.

flashcards.front: eBGP vs iBGP — what's different?
flashcards.back: eBGP runs between routers in different ASes; it's how the internet is glued together. iBGP runs between routers inside the same AS — it carries external routes to internal routers. iBGP requires a full mesh (or route reflectors) because routes learned via iBGP are NOT re-advertised to other iBGP peers.

flashcards.front: What is AS_PATH and why does it matter?
flashcards.back: AS_PATH is the list of autonomous systems a route has traversed, prepended at each AS boundary. It's the primary loop-prevention mechanism (a router rejects a route already containing its own AS) and the second tie-breaker in BGP best-path selection — shorter path wins.

flashcards.front: BGP best-path attributes — name the top three.
flashcards.back: (1) Highest LOCAL_PREF wins (locally configured 'prefer this exit'). (2) Shortest AS_PATH. (3) Lowest ORIGIN code (IGP < EGP < incomplete). Then MED, then eBGP > iBGP, then lowest IGP cost, then router-ID tie-breaker. LOCAL_PREF is how you steer outbound; AS_PATH prepending is how you influence inbound.

flashcards.front: Why does BGP need a route reflector?
flashcards.back: iBGP requires a full mesh (every router peers with every other) — O(n²) sessions, doesn't scale. A route reflector breaks the rule: it re-advertises iBGP routes to its clients. Clients only peer with the RR. One RR + 100 clients = 100 sessions vs. 5,000 for a full mesh.

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of AS Path prepending in BGP?
pairs.option: Makes a route less preferred by artificially lengthening the AS path attribute — used to influence inbound traffic when multihomed to multiple ISPs

pairs.stem: What is BGP Weight attribute and how does it differ from Local Preference?
What is Cisco NSF/GR (Graceful Restart) for BGP?
What is BGP route reflection and why is it needed?
pairs.option: Solves the iBGP full mesh requirement.

pairs.stem: What is BGP communities attribute?
pairs.option: A well-known or private transitive attribute tagging BGP routes with 32-bit values to influence routing policy across AS boundaries — used for filtering, preference, and route manipulation

pairs.stem: What is the BGP MED (Multi-Exit Discriminator) attribute and how is it used?

nodes.title: Mpls: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mpls. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is MPLS Label Distribution Protocol (LDP)?
flashcards.back: LDP (or TDP, RSVP-TE for traffic engineering) establishes label-to-FEC (Forwarding Equivalency Class) bindings between Label Switching Routers. Each LSR maintains a Label Information Base (LIB) and forwards packets using label lookup.

flashcards.front: What is MPLS TE (Traffic Engineering)?
flashcards.back: MPLS TE uses RSVP-TE to signal explicit LSPs. Routers run OSPF-TE/IS-IS-TE (with TE extensions to share bandwidth info). Offline computation or PCEP/SDN controllers calculate optimal paths. Used for WAN optimization and congestion avoidance.

flashcards.front: What is VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service)?
flashcards.back: VPLS creates a distributed virtual switch across provider MPLS network. All customer sites appear in same L2 domain. Uses PWs (pseudowires) between PE routers. Replaced increasingly by EVPN which provides the same service more efficiently.

flashcards.front: What is MPLS PHP (Penultimate Hop Popping)?
flashcards.back: PHP: implicit null label (3) signals penultimate router to pop. Egress LSR does only IP lookup, not MPLS+IP. Ultimate Hop Popping (UHP): explicit null label (0) — label kept until egress for QoS or tracking purposes.

pairs.stem: What is MPLS Label Distribution Protocol (LDP)?
pairs.option: Distributes MPLS labels between neighbor LSRs so that packets can be forwarded based on labels rather than IP lookups throughout the MPLS network

pairs.stem: What is MPLS TE (Traffic Engineering)?
pairs.option: Extends MPLS to route traffic along explicitly specified paths (LSPs) based on bandwidth constraints and optimization goals, rather than following the IGP shortest path

pairs.stem: What is MPLS L3VPN and how are customer routes kept separate?
What is MPLS PHP (Penultimate Hop Popping)?
What is VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service)?
pairs.option: An MPLS/IP service providing multipoint Layer 2 Ethernet bridging across a provider network — connects multiple sites in a single broadcast domain as if directly connected on the same LAN

pairs.stem: What is MPLS LDP session protection?

nodes.title: IP routing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Routing is how packets find their way through a multi-network internet. Every router runs a forwarding table; routing protocols (OSPF, EIGRP, BGP) are the mechanisms by which routers exchange information and build that table.

flashcards.front: What's the longest-prefix-match rule?
flashcards.back: When multiple routes match a destination, the router picks the one with the most-specific (longest) prefix. So `10.0.0.0/24` beats `10.0.0.0/16` for a packet to `10.0.0.5`. This is how more-specific routes can override defaults.

flashcards.front: Default route — what does `0.0.0.0/0` mean?
flashcards.back: It matches every destination, so it's used only when no more-specific route exists. Typically points to the internet gateway. On a stub network, the default route is often the ONLY route — everything not local goes 'up' to a smarter router.

flashcards.front: Static vs dynamic routing — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Static routes are hand-configured, easy to understand, perfect for small or stub networks. Dynamic routing (OSPF, BGP, EIGRP) auto-discovers topology, reacts to link failures, scales to thousands of routers. Use dynamic the moment the topology is non-trivial or expected to change.

flashcards.front: Administrative distance — what is it?
flashcards.back: When the same destination is learned from multiple sources (static + OSPF + BGP), the router prefers the one with the lowest administrative distance. Defaults (Cisco): connected=0, static=1, EIGRP=90, OSPF=110, BGP=200. It's the tie-breaker before the routing-protocol metric.

pairs.stem: What is VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding)?
pairs.option: Creates multiple independent routing tables on a single router, allowing overlapping IP address spaces and complete routing isolation between customers or VPNs

pairs.stem: What is IS-IS and how does it compare to OSPF?
What is PBR (Policy-Based Routing)?
What is BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection)?
pairs.option: A lightweight, rapid failure detection protocol providing sub-second hello timers to detect link or path failures faster than routing protocol timers

pairs.stem: What is OSPF route redistribution and what must be considered?
What is Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) routing?
pairs.option: Load balancing across multiple paths with equal cost metrics — packets distributed across all equal-cost next-hops for a destination. Supported by OSPF, EIGRP, IS-IS, BGP (with policy)

nodes.title: Cisco: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Cisco. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is Cisco SD-Access and its key components?
flashcards.back: SD-Access: Underlay (routed access), Overlay (VXLAN/LISP), Policy (ISE+SGT/SGACLs), Management (DNA Center). Virtual Networks (VNs) provide macro-segmentation; Scalable Group Tags (SGTs) provide micro-segmentation.

flashcards.front: What is Cisco IOS-XE, IOS-XR, and NX-OS?
flashcards.back: IOS-XE: modular architecture (SPA/SIP separation), enterprise-grade. IOS-XR: microkernel, in-service software upgrade (ISSU), massive scale, 32-bit process separation. NX-OS: Linux-based, programmable, feature-rich for data center.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Cisco DNA Assurance?
flashcards.back: DNA Assurance provides 360° network visibility with AI-driven insights, AI-driven issue detection, client health scores, application performance monitoring, and natural language search for troubleshooting.

flashcards.front: What is IP SLA in Cisco IOS?
flashcards.back: IP SLA: 'ip sla 1' define operation (icmp-echo, udp-jitter). 'ip sla schedule'. 'show ip sla statistics'. Track SLA with 'track 1 ip sla 1 reachability' → use in routing: 'ip route ... track 1' (floating static based on reachability).

pairs.stem: What is Cisco IOS-XE, IOS-XR, and NX-OS?
pairs.option: IOS-XE: modular IOS for enterprise routers/switches (ASR, ISR). IOS-XR: carrier-grade, high-availability OS for service provider routers (ASR 9K, CRS). NX-OS: data center OS for Nexus switches (feature-rich, Linux-based)

pairs.stem: What is IP SLA in Cisco IOS?
pairs.option: Active measurement tool generating synthetic traffic (ICMP echo, UDP jitter, HTTP, DNS) to measure network performance (latency, jitter, packet loss) — used for troubleshooting, routing decisions via object tracking, and SLA verification

pairs.stem: What is Cisco APIC-EM vs Catalyst Center (DNA Center)?
What is Cisco SD-Access and its key components?
What is a Cisco Catalyst switch stackwise vs VSS vs vPC?
What is the purpose of Cisco DNA Assurance?
pairs.option: Uses AI/ML to continuously monitor network health, identify anomalies, correlate issues across devices, and provide guided remediation with root cause analysis

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is EIGRP DUAL (Diffusing Update Algorithm)?
flashcards.back: DUAL runs in EIGRP to select loop-free routes. It maintains the Successor (best path) and Feasible Successors (backup paths meeting FC). Avoids Dijkstra's CPU-intensive SPF calculation while guaranteeing loop-free convergence.

flashcards.front: What is EIGRP named mode and its advantages?
flashcards.back: Named EIGRP: 'router eigrp NAME' with address-family sections. Wide metrics use 64-bit composite (supports >100Gbps links properly). Backward compatible. All new EIGRP configurations should use named mode.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of EIGRP Stub routing?
flashcards.back: EIGRP stub router (spoke): 'eigrp stub connected summary'. Hub won't send Queries to stub routers (can't be used as transit). Reduces query domain scope dramatically in large hub-and-spoke topologies, preventing SIA (Stuck In Active) scenarios.

flashcards.front: What is EIGRP Unequal-Cost Load Balancing?
flashcards.back: EIGRP variance: 'variance 2' means install routes with metric up to 2x Successor metric (must meet Feasibility Condition). Traffic proportional: route with metric 1000 gets 2x traffic of route with metric 2000. Unique EIGRP feature — OSPF only supports ECMP.

pairs.stem: What is CDP vs LLDP security risk and mitigation?
What is Cisco Flexible NetFlow?
What is a GRE tunnel?
What is Cisco DNA Spaces and location services integration?
What is a network fabric in modern data center design?
pairs.option: A highly scalable Leaf-Spine topology where every leaf connects to every spine, providing equal-cost multi-path routing, predictable latency, and easy horizontal scaling

pairs.stem: What is SD-WAN and what problem does it solve?
pairs.option: Software-Defined WAN — decouples WAN networking from hardware, enabling centralized policy-based management across multiple WAN transports (MPLS, broadband, LTE) with automatic path selection
